summary: Repeat prompt latency regressions & intermittent request timeouts caused by KV/prefix cache behavior
description:
Issue summary: Customers observed higher-than-expected latency and occasional request timeouts for repeated prompts (same user prompt sent multiple times). Impact: NovaDocs experienced increased tail latency leading to degraded UX and 504s on ~2% of repeat requests. Environment: Production serving pool in us-east, traffic routed to dedicated capacity for NovaDocs.

Observed behaviour: For identical prompt sequences sent within short intervals (~10s-2m), cold-run latency was expected only on first request and subsequent repeats should be significantly faster due to KV/prefix cache. Instead, repeat requests frequently exhibited similar latency to cold runs and some requests timed out (504).

Expected behaviour: Repeat prompts should benefit from KV cache warm state and be ~30-60% faster than cold runs with no timeouts.

Impact classification: P1 customer-impacting latency regression affecting a single dedicated customer but with potential platform-wide implications.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovaDocs dedicated API key against us-east endpoint
2) Send identical prompt payloads in quick succession (5-120s apart) at small scale (1-5 concurrent requests)
3) Observe per-request latency and status codes. Repeat requests should be significantly faster but were observed to have similar latency or return 504 on ~2% of attempts
4) Check serving runtime metrics: KV cache hit rate, prefix_cache.evictions, runtime_per_token_latency on the same node

investigation_notes: 2026-02-26 16:00 — Support triage: Reproduced high tail latency on repeat prompts in customer’s dedicated pool. Observed low KV cache hit rates (30-40%) where expected >70% for repeated prompts.

Hypothesis A: KV/prefix cache eviction policy became more aggressive after recent change to cache memory accounting (PR #4321) causing premature evictions of prefix caches for sessions with low memory weight.

Hypothesis B: Interaction between autoscaler and cache warming — nodes were scaled down aggressively, causing warmed caches to be lost; warm-up on scale-up is slower than before (PR #4338 touches scheduler heuristics).
Metric evidence: prefix_cache.evictions increased 3x starting 2026-02-26T14:40 UTC, coinciding with a deploy of PR #4321 to prod us-east cluster.
Trace evidence: Traces show KV lookup falling back to recompute path frequently, adding ~700-1200ms per request on average compared to cache-hit path.

Customer impact: NovaDocs reported increased 504s and UX degradation between 14:45-16:30 UTC. No other major customers on same pool reported during window but metrics show global slight increase in eviction rates in us-east.
Temporary mitigation: Increased cache size limit for NovaDocs dedicated pool and pinned capacity to prevent immediate scale-down. Applied at 2026-02-26T17:05 UTC via emergency config change.

Root cause: A change to memory accounting in PR #4321 underestimated per-prefix memory weight for certain tokenizers, causing the eviction policy to evict prefixes more aggressively under the same memory pressure. This was compounded by autoscaler scaling decisions post-PR #4338.

resolution: Root cause: regression introduced by change to cache memory accounting (PR #4321) which undercounted per-prefix memory in some tokenizer paths, triggering higher-than-expected prefix evictions and causing repeat prompts to behave like cold runs. Fix: corrected memory accounting and adjusted eviction thresholds in PR #4338. Rollout: staged deploy to us-east on 2026-03-01 with canary nodes then full pool. Post-deploy metrics show prefix_cache.hit_rate restored from ~38% to ~78% for affected traffic and latency returned to expected baselines. Follow-ups: add unit tests for tokenizer memory accounting, add metric alert for sudden prefix_eviction rate increases, and update autoscaler heuristics to consider recent cache-warmth signal. Workaround applied during incident: increased cache quota and disabled rapid scale-down for NovaDocs dedicated pool.
